Team — passing along Bluefin's redlines (attached earlier). High level asks below; need your callouts so my counter can be operationally realistic and acceptable to procurement/legal. Please reply inline or provide a short note by EOD Friday (24 Jul).

Bluefin requests (summary):
- 99.95% monthly uptime; sliding service credits starting at 99.90%
- P1 response windows: 1 hour (business hours), 4 hours (after hours)
- 30-day maintenance notice; cap 8 maintenance hours/month
- 12-month audit/log retention + right to request exports

My preliminary thoughts and questions:
- Uptime target: 99.95% for multi-tenant hosted API is tighter than Redwood's standard 99.9% for the hosted tier. Dedicated/private deployments can reach 99.95% under reserved capacity. Recommend: offer 99.95% for Dedicated (reserved) customers, and 99.9% for Hosted with an optional elevated SLA addendum.

- Credits: prefer a capped monthly credit pool (e.g., max 100% of monthly fees) rather than open-ended sliding scale. Suggest sample language: "Service Credit shall not exceed the Fees paid for the affected Service in the month."

- Response times: 1-hour P1 during business hours may be feasible with a paid Premium Support add-on; otherwise standard is 2-hour business-hours, 6-hour after-hours for hosted. Need Monica to confirm on-call cost and staffing delta for a 1-hour promise.

- Maintenance windows: 30-day notice is reasonable for planned maint; 8 hours/month is high unless we agree that small patching is excluded. Recommend: 14-day notice for minor maintenance, 30-day for major; cap of 6 hours/month standard, with an option to schedule additional hours for releases.

- Logs/audit: we can provide 12-month exports, but streaming access requires Private deployment with dedicated tooling. Also need to confirm redaction/PII handling and costs.

Action items:
- Rishi: please draft redline language for uptime/credit cap and rollback clauses.
- Monica: confirm incremental cost for 1-hour P1 SLA and whether CS can support remedial monitoring/bridging.
- Neha: prepare a short messaging plan for procurement — what we can concede vs. require as add-ons.

Thanks — I can draft the consolidated counter on 28 Jul once I have these inputs and will propose meeting times.

—Grace

Subject: Redwood counterproposal: SLA & support — v2 (attached)

Oliver / Eleanor — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Attached is Redwood_Counter_SLA_v2.docx with our consolidated positions and proposed compromise language. High level summary: 

1) Uptime & credits
- For Hosted (standard): 99.90% monthly uptime target; credits tiered starting at <99.85% with an overall monthly credit cap of 100% of monthly fees.
- For Dedicated/Private (reserved capacity): 99.95% monthly uptime; sliding credits starting at <99.9%.

2) P1 response times
- Standard hosted: 2-hour response during business hours, 6-hour after-hours
- Premium Support add-on: 1-hour business-hours response + 4-hour after-hours; includes a named escalation path and weekly status updates until resolution

3) Maintenance windows
- Planned maintenance: 14-day notice for minor changes, 30-day notice for major releases. Standard cap of 6 maintenance hours/month; additional windows can be scheduled as part of a release calendar with mutual agreement. Emergency maintenance excluded, with post-event communication and credits only if customer impact meets credit thresholds.

4) Logs & audit access
- Redwood will provide periodic exports up to 12 months for Hosted. Streaming or live log access available for Dedicated/Private via a dedicated project and associated fees. All exports will comply with our data retention and redaction policies.

Attachments: Redwood_Counter_SLA_v2.docx (contains exact clause language and suggested redline).

Proposed next step: 30-min alignment call on Fri 30 Jul at 10:00 AM ET to review the specific clause wording and agree on any follow-up legal changes. If that time doesn't work, please suggest alternatives.

If you need immediate clarifications, Rishi (legal) and Monica (CS) are on copy.
